topics.title: The Seventh Day
topics.subtitle: Why the Sabbath Was Never Done Away With, and Was Never Moved
topics.lede: There is no verse in Scripture that abolishes the Sabbath. There is no verse that moves it to the first day of the week. What exists is a handful of passages stretched to imply it, and a well documented history of men who changed it on their own authority.
topics.note: A printable teaching handout. Scripture quoted from the World English Bible with the Names restored: YHWH, Yahshua, Elohim. Torah is referred to throughout as instructions, which is what the word means.

items: The Sabbath was set apart at creation, roughly two thousand years before Abraham.
It was already being kept before Sinai, and YHWH rebuked Israel for breaking it before it was ever given at the mountain.
It is the only commandment of the ten that is treated as optional today, though it was written on the same stone by the same finger.
Yahshua kept it His whole life, called Himself its Lord, and expected His followers to still be keeping it long after His death.
The apostles kept it for decades after the resurrection, with Gentiles gathered alongside them.
Scripture says it is still being kept in the new heavens and the new earth.
Every passage used to abolish it, answered one at a time.
All eight first day verses in the Renewed Covenant, examined.
Where the change actually came from, in the documented record.

sections.heading: It Began at Creation, Before Israel Existed

blocks.v: Before there was a Jew, before there was a Hebrew, before there was a covenant at Sinai, before a single instruction was given to Moses, there was a seventh day.

“On the seventh day God finished his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.”

Three actions are taken on that day, and they are taken on nothing else in the creation week. He rested in it. He blessed it. He made it holy, which means He set it apart. He blessed the sea creatures and He blessed mankind, but only one thing in time itself is sanctified. He placed a holy day inside the week the same way He would later place a holy place inside the land.
If the Sabbath is only a Jewish institution, why is it in the garden roughly two thousand years before Abraham was born?
Yahshua Himself settles who it was made for.
“The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.”
It was made. Made when? Genesis 2. Made for whom? Man. Adam. Humanity. That is the entire species, not one nation out of it.

sections.heading: It Was Already Known Before Sinai

blocks.v: It is commonly taught that the Sabbath began at Mount Sinai. Scripture says otherwise. Israel was keeping it in the wilderness before they ever reached the mountain.

In Exodus 16:22-30, the manna falls. On the sixth day the people gather double. Moses tells them that the following day is a solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to YHWH. Some go out to gather anyway. Then comes the rebuke.
“YHWH said to Moses, ‘How long do you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?’”

This is Exodus 16. Sinai does not happen until Exodus 20. YHWH is rebuking Israel for breaking a commandment that, by the common teaching, had not been given yet. You cannot break a command that does not exist.

Exodus 16 is not the institution of the Sabbath. It is the reminder of it after four hundred years in Egypt. That is precisely why the Fourth Commandment opens with a word that no other commandment opens with.

sections.heading: He Wrote It With His Own Finger

blocks.v: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. You shall labor six days, and do all your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to YHWH your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates; for in six days YHWH made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore YHWH blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.”

items: Remember. Not begin. Not start. You remember something that already exists.
The reason given is creation, not Israel. The Fourth Commandment grounds itself in Genesis 2, which is why it cannot be a temporary national ordinance. Its foundation is the making of the world.
It is the longest of the ten, and the only one that identifies who YHWH is by what He made. It functions as the seal on the covenant.

blocks.v: Deuteronomy 5:12-15 repeats the ten and adds a second reason, the deliverance from Egypt. Two grounds are given: He made you, and He redeemed you. Both still apply to every person reading this.
“He gave to Moses … two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets, written with God’s finger.”

Nine of these ten are preached without hesitation in nearly every congregation in the country. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not commit adultery. Do not take His name in vain. Honor your father and mother. No one stands in a pulpit and argues that the commandment against idolatry was nailed to the cross.
Which finger of YHWH wrote the nine that stayed, and which finger wrote the one that was removed? It was the same finger, the same stone, the same moment, the same covenant.
“The children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel forever.”

A sign. Not a suggestion and not a shadow of a festival. In the same way tzitzit are a visible sign worn on the body, the Sabbath is a sign placed in time. It marks who you belong to. And the words used are not soft ones: perpetual, forever, throughout their generations.
“Moreover also I gave them my Sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am YHWH who sanctifies them.”
Ezekiel 20:20 repeats it. The Sabbath is how a person knows who sanctifies them. That is not ceremony. That is identity. Which is exactly why the enemy of your soul would want it removed.

sections.heading: It Was Never for Israel Alone

blocks.v: This is the objection you will hear most often, and Scripture answers it directly. The commandment itself, in Exodus 20:10, includes the stranger within your gates. The foreigner living among them rests as well.

“Also the foreigners who join themselves to YHWH, to serve him, and to love YHWH’s name, to be his servants, everyone who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and holds fast my covenant: I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer … for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”
Read the verses just before it. YHWH names the exact fear the foreigner carries, that he will be separated from His people, and He answers that fear with the Sabbath.
In Isaiah 56 the Sabbath is not the wall that keeps the nations out. It is the door that brings them in.
This is also the chapter Yahshua quotes when He cleanses the temple in Matthew 21:13. He knew this passage well.
“If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day; and call the Sabbath a delight … then you shall delight yourself in YHWH.”
A delight. Not a burden. That one word corrects most of what people assume this day is.

sections.heading: Yahshua Kept It, and Taught It

blocks.v: If the Sabbath were going to be moved or cancelled, the ministry of the Messiah is where it would have happened. It did not.
“He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.”
As was his custom. This was His lifelong, normal pattern. The one we are told to imitate did not have a Sunday.
“Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

This verse is used to argue that He abolished it. He said the opposite. A man is not lord of something he deleted. He is Lord of the Sabbath, which means it is His day. If the seventh day is His day, whose day is the first?

“Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill. For most certainly, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letter or one tiny pen stroke shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished. Whoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments and shall teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven.”

items: Heaven and earth are still here. Look outside.
He said not one stroke of a pen. The Sabbath commandment is ninety four words in English. That is considerably more than a pen stroke.
He specifically warned about teaching others to break the least of them. The Sabbath is not the least. It is one of the ten.

blocks.v: “Pray that your flight will not be in the winter, nor on a Sabbath.”

Here Yahshua describes events unfolding decades and centuries after His death and resurrection, and He still assumes His followers are keeping the Sabbath. If it were about to be abolished at the cross, the instruction is meaningless.
“They returned and prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.”

The people closest to Him, who had followed Him to the execution and to the tomb, rested on the Sabbath according to the commandment. No one had told them anything changed, because nothing had. Notice what the Gospel writer still calls it: the commandment.
There were two Sabbaths that week
This passage is often read through a Friday crucifixion, which flattens the week and hides something important. The Sabbath that began at the burial was not the weekly one.
“Therefore the Jews, because it was the Preparation Day, so that the bodies wouldn’t remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a high day) …”

A high day. That is an annual Sabbath, the first day of Unleavened Bread, commanded in Leviticus 23:6-7 as a holy convocation on which no regular work is done. It falls on whatever weekday the calendar puts it, independent of the seventh day.

Now put two verses side by side, because together they cannot fit into one Sabbath. Mark 16:1 says that when the Sabbath was past, the women bought spices. Luke 23:56 says they prepared spices and then rested on the Sabbath. Buying comes after a Sabbath. Resting comes after the preparing. You cannot buy after the Sabbath and also rest after the preparing unless there are two Sabbaths with a working day between them.

The high Sabbath of Unleavened Bread came first. A working day followed, on which the women bought and prepared the spices. Then came the weekly seventh day Sabbath, and on that one they rested according to the commandment. Two Sabbaths, one week.

This is also what makes the sign He gave possible. He said the only sign given would be the sign of Jonah, three days and three nights in the heart of the earth (Matthew 12:40). A Wednesday evening burial to the close of the weekly Sabbath is three full days and three full nights. A Friday afternoon burial cannot produce three nights no matter how the hours are counted.

And it puts the empty tomb exactly where the calendar says it belongs. Leviticus 23:10-11 sets the wave sheaf of firstfruits on the day after the Sabbath, and Paul says Messiah has been raised as the firstfruits of those who are asleep (1 Corinthians 15:20). The women come while it is still dark on the first day and find the stone already rolled away and the tomb already empty (John 20:1).

For this teaching the point is simple. Even in the week of the crucifixion, with an annual high Sabbath already observed, the seventh day Sabbath was still kept, and Scripture still calls it the commandment.

Every conflict Yahshua had over the Sabbath was with man made rules about the day, never with the day itself. He healed on it. He picked grain on it. He declared it lawful to do good on it in Matthew 12:12. He was correcting how it was kept, not whether it was kept. If your Sabbath teaching becomes a burden of rules, you have made the exact error He was fighting.

sections.heading: The Disciples Kept It After the Resurrection

blocks.v: If the day changed at the cross, the book of Acts is the wrong book to have in your Bible.

rows.v: Paul and Barnabas go into the synagogue on the Sabbath day.
Gentiles beg to hear these words again. Paul tells them the next Sabbath, and they wait a full week. Then almost the whole city gathers on the Sabbath.
In Philippi there is no synagogue. Paul keeps the Sabbath anyway, outside the city by a river.
“Paul, as was his custom, went in to them, and for three Sabbaths reasoned with them from the Scriptures.” The same phrase used of Yahshua in Luke 4:16.
He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, persuading Jews and Greeks, and stayed a year and six months. That is roughly seventy eight consecutive Sabbaths with a mixed congregation.
About twenty five years after the resurrection, James states that the rumor Paul teaches against Torah is not true, and has Paul prove it publicly.
“I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets.”
“Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”
“I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers.”

blocks.v: Acts 13:42-44 is the moment that settles it. Paul has a room full of brand new Gentile believers asking him when to come back. If the day of assembly had been moved to the first day of the week, this is where he says so. He does not. He tells them next Sabbath, and they wait seven days.

sections.heading: It Is Still Being Kept After This Age Ends

blocks.v: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says YHWH, “so your offspring and your name shall remain. It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” says YHWH.

A shadow that was supposedly fulfilled and discarded does not reappear in eternity. In Ezekiel's temple vision the Sabbath is likewise observed, the east gate is opened on it, and the people worship at that gate (Ezekiel 44:24; 45:17;
“There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God. For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.”

The Greek word in verse 9 is sabbatismos, and it occurs nowhere else in the Renewed Covenant. It literally means a Sabbath keeping. The writer, addressing believers, says one remains. Not was. Not used to be. Remains. The rest we enter in Messiah does not cancel the day, it fills it with meaning.

sections.heading: The Passages Used to Say It Was Done Away With

blocks.v: Before working through them, notice what does not exist. There is no verse that says the Sabbath is abolished. There is no verse that says the seventh day is no longer holy. There is no verse that says to assemble on the first day instead. What exists is a handful of passages stretched to imply it.
Colossians 2:16-17
The claim: Paul says the Sabbath no longer matters.

items: Paul says do not let anyone judge you for keeping them. He is defending the observers, not the abstainers. If no one in Colossae had been keeping these days, there would have been nothing to be judged for.

Feast, new moon, and Sabbath is a standard Hebrew phrase for the whole worship calendar. See 1 Chronicles 23:31, 2 Chronicles 2:4 and 31:3, Nehemiah 10:33, Ezekiel 45:17. Paul is quoting Scripture, not cancelling it.
“Are a shadow” is present tense. A shadow proves a body exists. You do not discard the shadow that points to Messiah.

Verses 8 and 22 name the actual problem: the tradition of men, and the commandments and teachings of men. The issue in Colossae was human philosophy, asceticism, and angel worship in verse 18, not Torah.

blocks.v: Romans 14:5-6
The claim: Every believer may choose whichever day he prefers.

items: The chapter is about eating and fasting. Read verses 2, 3, 6, 14, 15, 17 and 21. It concerns meat, vegetables, and wine, in a congregation with weak and strong consciences.
The Sabbath is never mentioned in the chapter. Not once. It has to be imported.
The days most likely in view are voluntary fast days. Nothing here overturns a commandment written in stone that Paul himself kept every week in Acts 17 and 18. Paul does not contradict Paul.

blocks.v: Galatians 4:9-11
The claim: Paul rebukes them for keeping the appointed times.

items: Verse 8 identifies the audience: when they did not know God they were in bondage to those who by nature are not gods. These were pagan Gentiles. Paul describes what they are turning back to, and you cannot turn back to something you were never in. They had never been Sabbath keepers.
The days, months, seasons and years in view are the pagan calendar and the elemental spirits, not YHWH’s appointed times.
The entire letter concerns circumcision as a means of salvation. See 5:2-4 and 6:12-13. It is a justification argument, not a calendar argument.

blocks.v: 2 Corinthians 3 and Hebrews 8
The claim: The old covenant is obsolete, so the Sabbath is obsolete.

items: The renewed covenant is defined in Jeremiah 31:33 and quoted in Hebrews 8:10: “I will put my laws into their mind, I will also write them on their heart.” The same instructions, moved from stone to heart. The renewed covenant is not the removal of His instructions. It is the internalizing of them.
What faded in 2 Corinthians 3 was the glory on the face of Moses and the ministration of condemnation, not the definition of righteousness.
If the renewed covenant deleted the commandments, then adultery and murder are permitted as well. No one actually believes this.

blocks.v: “We are under grace, not law”
What it says

rows.v: Empty tomb discovery on the first day. The women find the stone already rolled away and the tomb already empty. It records the discovery, not the moment of the rising. No change of day.
Empty tomb discovery on the first day. The women find the stone already rolled away and the tomb already empty. It records the discovery, not the moment of the rising. No change of day.
A summary statement about the first day appearances. Even here the day is narrative, not instruction. No change of day.
Empty tomb discovery on the first day. The women find the stone already rolled away and the tomb already empty. It records the discovery, not the moment of the rising. No change of day.
Empty tomb discovery on the first day. The women find the stone already rolled away and the tomb already empty. It records the discovery, not the moment of the rising. No change of day.
The evening of the first day. The disciples are gathered with the doors locked “for fear of the Jews.” A frightened group hiding, not a worship service establishing a new day.

The strongest verse anyone has. Paul is departing in the morning, preaches until midnight, Eutychus falls, Paul raises him, and they talk until daybreak. Reckoned evening to evening, this begins Saturday night at the close of Sabbath. It is a farewell gathering for a departing apostle, and breaking bread happened daily anyway per Acts 2:46.

A private setting aside of money at home for the famine relief in Jerusalem, so no collections are needed when Paul arrives. The text says each one by himself. No assembly, no service, no worship mentioned.

items: Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? May it never be.
Do we nullify the law through faith? May it never be. We establish the law.
The law is holy, and the commandment holy, righteous, and good.
One who says he knows him and does not keep his commandments is a liar.
This is loving God, that we keep his commandments, and they are not grievous.
Here is the perseverance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Yahshua.
The dragon makes war with those who keep God’s commandments and hold the testimony of Yahshua.

blocks.v: Grace is what saves us. Obedience is what love looks like afterward. We do not keep the seventh day in order to be redeemed. We keep it because we have been redeemed, and this is what our Redeemer said He wanted.

sections.heading: All Eight First Day Verses, Examined

blocks.v: There are exactly eight verses in the entire Renewed Covenant that mention the first day of the week. Six describe the same single morning. Not one commands worship on that day.
Revelation 1:10 “The Lord’s day.” Nothing in the verse says the first day. We already know from Yahshua which day He claimed as His: “The Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
Eight verses. Zero commands. Zero changes.
Since Scripture does not move the day, something else did. And the institution that made the change does not deny it. It is stated plainly in their own official teaching.
Catechism of the Catholic Church, 2175 and 2190

Paragraph 2175 states that Sunday is expressly distinguished from the sabbath which it follows chronologically every week, and that for Christians its ceremonial observance replaces that of the sabbath. Paragraph 2190 states that the sabbath, which represented the completion of the first creation, has been replaced by Sunday.

Read those carefully. They are not claiming Scripture moved the day. They are stating that the practice of the Church replaced it. Both paragraphs can be read directly on vatican.va, which is exactly why these are the two citations to use. Always use the source a person can verify for themselves.
Constantine’s edict, March 7, 321 AD

The first civil law making the first day a rest day across the Roman Empire came from the emperor, not from Scripture. It commanded that judges, city people, and all workshops rest on the venerable day of the Sun, while permitting farm work to continue. The law does not call it the Lord's day. It calls it the day of the Sun, the solar terminology of Rome, dies Solis, from Sol Invictus. Constantine at that time still held the office of Pontifex Maximus, high priest of Rome's traditional religion.
The Council of Laodicea, Canon 29, around 364 AD

This canon instructed that Christians should not rest on the Sabbath in the manner of the Jews, but should work that day and honor the Lord's day instead, and stated that those who persisted in resting on the Sabbath were to be cut off from Messiah.

This is the hinge. It does not merely promote one day. It forbids the seventh and threatens those who keep it. You do not need a law against something no one is doing. Canon 29 is proof that believers were still resting on the seventh day three hundred years after the resurrection, and had to be legislated out of it.
“He shall speak words against the Most High, and shall wear out the saints of the Most High. He shall plan to change the times and the law.”
“In vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men … You set aside the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.”
“First day gatherings existed before Constantine.”
They did, and it does not touch the argument, because gathering is not resting. Do not let anyone slide those two together. They are different things, and the early record keeps them separate.

items: Justin Martyr, around 150 AD, describes an assembly on the day of the sun. People coming together to read, pray, and share a meal. He does not describe anyone ceasing from labor, and he does not call it a Sabbath. No one in that era did.

Pliny the Younger, writing to Trajan around 112 AD, describes Christians meeting on a fixed day before daylight and then dispersing to their ordinary business. You meet before work, then you go to work. That is a meeting scheduled around a work day, not a day of rest.

The commandment is not “attend a service.” The commandment is cease from your labor and keep the day holy. The early believers gathered constantly, daily according to Acts 2:46, and none of it was ever a substitute for the seventh day.

blocks.v: And here is the proof they were doing both for centuries. Socrates Scholasticus, writing in the fifth century, records that almost all churches throughout the world were still assembling on the Sabbath every week, and that Alexandria and Rome had ceased to do so on account of some ancient tradition. Sozomen, writing around the same period, says the people of Constantinople and almost everywhere assembled on the Sabbath as well as on the first day, and that this was never the custom at Rome or Alexandria. (Socrates, Ecclesiastical History 5.22; Sozomen, Ecclesiastical History 7.19)

Four hundred years after the resurrection, most of the Christian world was still keeping the seventh day. Two cities were not: Rome and Alexandria. The historians who report it treat those two as the exception, not the rule.
So the timeline is clean.

items: First day gatherings appear early, and take nothing away from the seventh day.
The first law transferring rest to the first day is Constantine’s, March 7, 321.
The first church law forbidding the Sabbath rest is Laodicea, Canon 29, around 364.
Most of the world kept both into the fifth century, until Rome’s practice was imposed.

blocks.v: No one stopped resting on the seventh day because Scripture told them to. They stopped because they were legislated out of it, and it took centuries of pressure to finish the job.
Where critics do have a foothold

Two early writings, Ignatius in his letter to the Magnesians around 110 AD and the Epistle of Barnabas around 130 AD, use language about no longer sabbatizing. Handle them honestly. Barnabas is anonymous, was never received as Scripture, and is full of allegory no one today defends. In the Ignatius passage the Greek does not actually contain the word day. It reads as living according to the Lord's, and translators supply day to make it read “the Lord's day.” Verify it yourself before saying it publicly. Even taken at their worst, these are two men writing after the apostles were gone, with no authority to unholy what YHWH made holy.

No apostle, no prophet, and no word from Yahshua ever authorized the change. Every source for it is post apostolic and human. Trace it back as far as you like, you will never arrive at a “thus says YHWH.”
“You are being legalistic.”

Answer this one from the heart rather than the argument. We are not saved by a day. We are saved by the blood of Yahshua. We keep the day because we love Him, and because He said it was holy and no man has the authority to unholy it. Isaiah 58 calls it a delight. Mark 2 says it was made for man, as a gift. A gift is not legalism.
Do not turn this into a rulebook. That is the exact error Yahshua rebuked.

rows.topic: When. Sunset to sunset. Friday evening to Saturday evening.
rows.v: Genesis 1:5; Leviticus 23:32

rows.topic: Prepare ahead. The sixth day is preparation day. Cook, clean, run the errands. The peace of the day is built the day before.
rows.v: Exodus 16:23

rows.topic: Rest from your work, not from doing good. He healed on it and called it lawful to do good on it.
rows.v: Exodus 20:9-10; Matthew 12:12

rows.topic: Make it holy, which means set apart. It should not look like Tuesday. Word, prayer, worship, family, rest.
rows.v: Exodus 20:8

rows.topic: Gather. A holy convocation is a called assembly. Even if it is only your household around the table.
rows.v: Leviticus 23:3; Hebrews 10:25

rows.topic: Call it a delight. Good food, no work talk, no arguing. If your children grow up dreading it, something has gone wrong in how you keep it, not in the day.
rows.v: Isaiah 58:13

rows.topic: Walk in mercy. If someone in your life does not see this yet, love them. Do not weaponize the day.
rows.v: Micah 6:8; Romans 14:4

items: The prophets say all flesh will keep it in the new heavens and the new earth.
Hebrews says a Sabbath keeping remains for the people of God.

blocks.v: And nowhere, in a single verse, does He ever say to stop. Men changed it. Men do not have that authority.
Rest is not a burden He laid on you. It is a gift He gave you before you ever existed, and a sign of whose you are. It is a weekly appointment with your Creator that He wrote into time itself.
Come home to the seventh day.

topics.title: Sabbath, Fire, and Food
topics.subtitle: Why Context Decides the Meaning
topics.lede: The seventh day Sabbath still stands. It was never done away with and it was never moved. That is not the question here. The question is narrower: does Scripture forbid cooking, lighting a fire, or leaving your house on the Sabbath day?
topics.note: A printable teaching handout. Scripture quoted from the World English Bible with the Names restored: YHWH, Yahshua, Elohim. Torah is referred to throughout as instructions, which is what the word means.

items: Exodus 16 never issues a command not to cook. Every instruction in the chapter is attached to manna.
“Let no man go out of his place” is about going out to gather, not about staying inside the house.
Exodus 35:3 sits at the front of the Tabernacle building project, and every craft named in that chapter runs on fire.
Exodus 12:16 carves food preparation out of the definition of work on a High Sabbath, in YHWH’s own words.
Yahshua left His house, traveled, taught, and ate on the Sabbath, and was never once charged with breaking Torah for it.
The three objections you will actually hear, answered plainly, including the man gathering sticks in Numbers 15.
What the day is actually for, once the fences come down.

blocks.v: Exodus 16 is the first time Israel is ever taught anything about the Sabbath, and every instruction in the chapter is attached to one thing: manna. Read the verse people quote, and watch what it actually does.

“This is what YHWH has spoken: ‘Tomorrow is a solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to YHWH. Bake that which you want to bake, and boil that which you want to boil; and all that remains over lay up for yourselves to be kept until the morning.’”

That verse does not say do not cook. It says prepare ahead, because no manna would fall the next day. It is a supply instruction, not a fire prohibition. The reason given in the text itself is in verse 26: six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there shall be none.
Notice what is missing. There is no penalty attached to cooking in Exodus 16, and no command against it. The only rebuke in the chapter falls on the people who went out to gather on the seventh day.
“The children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate the manna until they came to the borders of the land of Canaan.”

That is the shelf life of the instruction. Manna was supernatural bread that fell for forty years and then stopped, in Joshua 5:12, the day after they ate the produce of the land. An instruction about how to handle manna cannot outlive the manna it was given for.

sections.heading: “Let No Man Go Out of His Place”

blocks.v: “Behold, because YHWH has given you the Sabbath, therefore he gives you on the sixth day the bread of two days. Everyone stay in his place. Let no one go out of his place on the seventh day.”

Pulled out by itself, this reads like house arrest. Read it with the verse before it and the situation is obvious. In verse 27, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather, and found nothing. That is the entire occasion for the command.

Go out where? Out to the field. Out to gather. YHWH is telling them not to go looking for bread that will not be there. The whole sentence is built on the manna: because He gives you two days of bread on the sixth, stay put on the seventh.
If this were a universal ban on leaving the house, Israel could never attend a holy convocation, which Leviticus 23:3 commands on that very day. A called assembly requires people to travel to it.
“He said, ‘Why would you want to go to him today? It is not a new moon or Sabbath.’”

Her husband is surprised she would go to the prophet on an ordinary day. Traveling to the man of God on the Sabbath or the new moon was so normal in Israel that it is the assumed background of the question. That one verse settles what Exodus 16:29 was never saying.
“You shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations on the Sabbath day.”
This is the verse that carries the whole no cooking position. So read the next verse. And the next thirty.

Exodus 35 is not a chapter about home life. It is the chapter where Moses gathers the whole assembly and gives them the instructions for building the Tabernacle. Beginning in verse 4 and running to the end of the chapter: gold, silver, bronze, engraving, casting, cutting, metal work, and the naming of Bezalel and Oholiab as the craftsmen.

items: Every one of those crafts runs on fire. Furnaces, forges, smelting, casting.
The Sabbath command in verses 1 through 3 is placed at the front of the building project, in one breath: remember the Sabbath, kindle no fire, now here is the work you are about to begin.
The fire being restrained is the fire of the workmen. It is a guard against a nation so zealous to build something for YHWH that they work straight through His rest.

blocks.v: The command is not sitting in a chapter about supper. It is sitting at the head of a construction manual. Context is not a loophole. Context is how you find out what a sentence means.
A second layer worth noticing

This assembly comes directly after the golden calf. In Exodus 32:5-6, Aaron built an altar, proclaimed a feast, and the people offered burnt offerings and sat down to eat and drink. Idol worship in that world ran on fire and a sacrificial meal. Israel had just used fire and precious metal to build something YHWH never asked for.

Now Moses gathers them again, and the first words out of his mouth are the Sabbath and the fire, immediately followed by the gold and silver they will bring for the true dwelling place. The contrast is deliberate. Use the fire for what He asked for, and never at the cost of His day.
Either reading lands in the same place. The verse is not about warmth, light, or a hot meal with your family.
If fire on a holy day were forbidden across the board, YHWH would be contradicting Himself, because He commands fire on one.
“They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread … Don’t eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with fire.”

Not raw. Not boiled. Roasted with fire, and He specifies it twice so there is no mistaking it. Passover leads directly into the first day of Unleavened Bread, which is a High Sabbath. And here is what He says about work on that day.

“In the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no kind of work shall be done in them, except that which every man must eat, that only may be done by you.”
Read that exception again. The instruction itself carves food preparation out of the definition of work on a holy day. That is not rabbinic tradition and it is not a loophole. It is the text.

So we have a day where YHWH says rest and hold a holy convocation, and in the same sentence says you may prepare what you eat, and in the same chapter says roast it in fire. That is not a contradiction. That is Him telling us what work meant when He gave the instruction.
If Exodus 35:3 were a universal ban on fire, then Exodus 12 would put Israel in violation of Torah every single Passover, by direct command. YHWH does not legislate His own people into sin.
He is YHWH in the flesh. He gave the instruction at Sinai and He kept it perfectly. So watch what He actually did on the day.

rows.v: “He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day.” He leaves the house. This is His lifelong pattern.
In Capernaum on the Sabbath. Teaching, casting out a spirit, leaving the synagogue, walking into Simon’s house, healing his mother in law, who then serves them.
Walking through grainfields with His disciples plucking heads of grain to eat, because they were hungry.
He defends them by pointing out that the priests in the temple work on the Sabbath and are guiltless.
“For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.” A man is not Lord of a day He abolished, and He is not breaking His own day.
“Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.”
He heals a man and tells him to take up his mat and walk. The accusation that follows is a violation of their tradition, not of YHWH’s instructions.
“The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.”

blocks.v: Luke 4 alone ends the Exodus 16:29 argument. He left His house. He traveled. He entered other people’s homes. He sat down and was served a meal. If any of that broke the Sabbath, the sinless One sinned, and He did not.
Every conflict Yahshua had over the Sabbath was with man made rules about the day, never with the day itself. He was correcting how it was kept, not whether it was kept.
“Exodus 20:10 says do no work at all.”

It does, and Exodus 12:16 tells us what that never included. Preparing what you eat was carved out by YHWH Himself. Scripture also shows us plainly what did break the day: in Nehemiah 13:15-22 it is treading winepresses, loading donkeys, hauling burdens through the gates, and buying and selling. That is commerce and labor, not a family meal.
“What about the man gathering sticks in Numbers 15?”
This is the first thing you will be handed, so know it well.

items: and never mentions fire at all. The charge is the work of gathering, in the same wilderness and the same season as the manna gathering of Exodus 16.
done to him. This is a judgment being established, not a standing rule being applied.
high hand, in open defiance, despising the word of YHWH. That is the frame the account is placed in.

blocks.v: Numbers 15 is a case of open, defiant labor being judged. It is not a verse about a man warming his house or a family eating a hot meal.
“You are just looking for an excuse.”

The opposite. Adding fences YHWH never built is exactly how Israel arrived at the place where healing a man was called a violation, and Yahshua rebuked them for it. Guarding the day means keeping what He said. Not more, and not less. Every fence a man adds becomes a burden he eventually places on somebody else.
“In vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men … You set aside the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.”

sections.heading: What the Day Is Actually For

blocks.v: Strip away the fences and here is what is left, and it is plenty.

rows.topic: When. Sunset to sunset. Friday evening to Saturday evening.
rows.v: Genesis 1:5; Leviticus 23:32
Exodus 20:9-10

rows.topic: Do not cause others to work. Your household, your servants, the stranger in your gates.
rows.v: Exodus 20:10

rows.topic: Do not buy and do not sell. This is the commerce Scripture actually names.
rows.v: Nehemiah 13:15-22

rows.topic: Keep it holy, which means set apart. It should not look like Tuesday.
rows.v: Exodus 20:8

rows.topic: Gather. A holy convocation is a called assembly, even if it is only your household around the table.
rows.v: Leviticus 23:3; Hebrews 10:25

rows.topic: Do good. Healing, mercy, and helping are welcome on the day, not violations of it.
rows.v: Matthew 12:12

rows.topic: Call it a delight. Good food, no work talk, no arguing.
rows.v: Isaiah 58:13-14

blocks.v: “If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day; and call the Sabbath a delight … then you shall delight yourself in YHWH.”

A delight. Not a burden, not a test, not a day of counting steps and watching the stove. So we rest. We read the Word with our family. We worship. We eat well and we eat together. We do good. We close the day in His presence.
gather.
The Sabbath was made for man. When we turn it into a list of things that will get us in trouble, we have handed back the very rest He gave us.
Keep the day. Guard it, love it, set it apart, and do not let anyone put you under a rule your Father never wrote.

topics.title: Yom Teruah
topics.subtitle: The Appointed Season No One Can Miss
topics.note: A Midrash Study on the Day of Trumpets and the Return of Yahshua Scripture quoted from the World English Bible with the sacred names restored. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of YHWH.

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Yahshua said no one knows the day or the hour of his return. In the same discourse he said that those who watch the tree will know the season, and Paul said the day will not overtake the children of light like a thief. Both are true, and Yom Teruah is where they meet. It is the one appointed time YHWH placed on the first day of a month, on the day the moon is hidden, and marked with a trumpet blast. A day you cannot pin down, inside a season you cannot miss if you are watching.
Only two passages in the instructions of YHWH command this day. Both are short. Both are loaded.

YHWH spoke to Moses, saying, Speak to the children of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, shall be a solemn rest to you, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work; and you shall offer an offering made by fire to YHWH.
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work. It is a day of blowing of trumpets to you.

Now notice what is not there. There is no explanation. No historical event attached. No Passover lamb, no exodus, no wilderness booths. Every other appointed day in Leviticus 23 comes with a reason written into the text. This one comes with a sound and a silence.
That silence is not an oversight. It is the design of the day.
This is the foundation everything else rests on, so we build it slowly.
The word itself

The Hebrew word is moed, plural moedim. It does not mean holiday, and it does not mean festival in the way we use that word. It means an appointed time, a fixed season, a set meeting. It carries the sense of a rendezvous, a scheduled appearance, a meeting placed on the calendar by someone with the authority to place it there.
Elohim said, Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years.

That word seasons is moedim. On day four of creation, before there was a Hebrew, before there was an Israel, before there was a scroll of instructions, YHWH hung the sun and the moon in the sky and said they exist to mark his appointments.
The appointed times are not Jewish culture. They are written into the sky.
He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.
Whose feasts are they
YHWH spoke to Moses, saying, Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, The set feasts of YHWH, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my set feasts.

Read that last line again. My set feasts. He does not call them the feasts of Israel. He does not call them the feasts of the Jews. He signs his own name to them. They belong to YHWH. Israel was simply the household that was handed the calendar to keep.
These are the set feasts of YHWH, even holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed season.
In their appointed season. Not whenever it is convenient. Not on a date a council picked centuries later. In the season he set.

blocks.title: Season, Not Date
blocks.v: Here is the key that unlocks the whole study. A moed is a season, and a season has an arrival you can feel before you can pinpoint it. You do not need a calendar to know autumn is coming. The air changes. The light changes. The leaves turn. You know the season long before you could name the exact hour it began. That is the entire prophetic logic of this day.

Yom Teruah means the Day of Blowing, or more literally the Day of Shouting. The Hebrew teruah is a specific kind of sound. Not a smooth note. A broken, urgent, staccato blast. An alarm. A war cry. A shout.
Scripture uses teruah for several things, and every one of them preaches.
Teruah as alarm and assembly
In Numbers 10:1-10 YHWH commands two silver trumpets. Read carefully what they are for:

items: A long blast gathers the whole congregation to the door of the tent. Numbers 10:3
A teruah, the broken alarm blast, breaks the camp and moves it out. Numbers 10:5-6
A teruah in war means you will be remembered before YHWH your Elohim, and you will be saved from your

blocks.v: enemies. Numbers 10:9

items: And trumpets are blown in the day of your gladness, in your set feasts, and in the beginnings of your months.

blocks.v: Assembly. Movement. Remembrance. Deliverance. That is the vocabulary of the trumpet, and it is the vocabulary of the return of Yahshua.
Teruah as the sound that brings walls down
When they make a long blast with the ram's horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; and the wall of the city shall fall down flat.
The trumpet and the shout together bring down what looked permanent (Joshua 6:20).
Teruah as the sound of joy

items: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of Elohim shouted for joy. Job 38:7
At the laying of the foundation, the shout of joy and the weeping of the old men mixed together until no one could tell the two apart. Ezra 3:11-13

blocks.v: Joy and grief in the same sound. That is what a trumpet does to a heart that has been waiting a very long time.
Teruah as the sound of the King arriving
Elohim has gone up with a shout, YHWH with the sound of a trumpet.
Blessed are the people who know the joyful sound. They walk, YHWH, in the light of your face.
That phrase, the joyful sound, is teruah. Blessed are the people who know the sound. Not the people who know the date. The people who recognize the sound when they hear it.

sections.heading: Why It Is Called the Day No One Knows

blocks.v: The scriptural reason

Every appointed time in Leviticus 23 is anchored to a numbered day of a month. Passover is the fourteenth. Unleavened Bread runs the fifteenth through the twenty first. Yom Kippur is the tenth. Sukkot is the fifteenth.
Yom Teruah is the only moed that falls on the first day of a month.

And in Scripture a month begins with the new moon. The new moon is the one lunar phase that cannot be seen in advance. The moon goes dark. It is hidden. Then a sliver returns, and until witnesses confirm it, no one on the ground can say with certainty that the month has begun.
Blow the trumpet at the New Moon, at the full moon, on our feast day.
The Hebrew behind New Moon in that verse carries the sense of concealment, of the covering. The day the trumpet sounds is the day the moon is hidden.

Watch the pattern play out in real life. In 1 Samuel 20 David tells Jonathan, behold, tomorrow is the new moon. Then read verses 18 through 27 and notice that the observance runs across two days, because the exact moment the month began could not be nailed down in advance.
So the day itself, by its own design, is the day you have to watch for. It arrives in a known season, in a known month, but not on an hour any man can announce ahead of time.
Now the honest part

You will hear it taught that no man knows the day or hour was a common Jewish idiom for this feast, and that everyone in the first century would have heard Yahshua say it and immediately thought of Yom Teruah.
Be straight with people about this. That specific idiom claim is not written in Scripture. It comes from later rabbinic and traditional sources. We do not build doctrine on rabbinic tradition.

blocks.title: The Pattern Is Stronger Than The Tradition
blocks.v: We do not need tradition for this connection, because it is already in the text. The one appointed time that cannot be pinned to a knowable day is the appointed time of the trumpet. Yahshua says the day of his return is the day no one knows, and that he returns at a trumpet. You do not need a rabbi to connect those. You need a Bible and a lunar calendar.
The statement
But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
But of that day or that hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father. Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you do not know when the time is.
The parable that names the feast without naming it
Look at every element of Matthew 25:1-13, the ten virgins:

items: A bridegroom whose arrival time is not announced.
Ten who are waiting, all of whom believe they are ready.
Lamps and oil, the difference between profession and preparation.
A delay long enough that all ten fall asleep.
A cry at midnight, a shout in the dark, waking everyone at once.
A door that shuts.
And the closing line: watch therefore, for you do not know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is

blocks.v: coming. Matthew 25:13
A shout in the darkness that wakes the sleeping and separates the ready from the unready. That is a teruah.
The verse that changes everything
Right before Yahshua says no one knows the day, he says this:

Now from the fig tree learn this parable: When its branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near. Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.

See the fig tree and all the trees. When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near. Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that the Kingdom of Elohim is near.

blocks.title: The Whole Teaching In One Line
blocks.v: You will not know the day. You will know the season.
He did not offer that as a suggestion. He said you know. He expects it. A man who watches the tree knows summer is coming, and he still cannot tell you the hour summer started.
Failing to know the season is a rebuke

When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, A shower is coming, and so it happens. When a south wind blows, you say, There will be a scorching heat, and it happens. You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you do not interpret this time?

items: You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you cannot discern the signs of the times. Matthew
Because you did not know the time of your visitation. Luke 19:44

blocks.v: Jerusalem missed him. Not because the information was hidden, but because they were not watching the season. That warning lands on us too.
The clearest passage in Scripture on this

But concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need that anything be written to you. For you yourselves know well that the day of YHWH comes like a thief in the night... But you, brothers, are not in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief. You are all children of light and children of the day. We do not belong to the night, nor to darkness, so then let us not sleep, as the rest do, but let us watch and be sober.

Sit with this one. Paul says the day comes like a thief, and then immediately says it will not come like a thief to you. Why? Because you are not in darkness. Because you are watching. Because you know the times and the seasons.

The Greek word there is kairos, appointed season, the same idea used to render moed in the Greek Scriptures. The children of light know the moedim. That is the difference between being caught and being ready.
If therefore you will not watch, I will come as a thief, and you will not know what hour I will come on you.
Read the condition. If you will not watch. The thief language is conditional, and the condition is watchfulness (see also Revelation 16:15).
Holding the tension honestly
It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.

Someone will bring this verse to you. Handle it plainly. The disciples were asking for a restoration schedule so they could sit down and calculate. Yahshua refused to feed date setting. He did not cancel watchfulness, because Matthew 24, Matthew 25, Mark 13, and 1 Thessalonians 5 all command it.

blocks.title: Draw The Line Here
blocks.v: Date setting is forbidden. Season watching is commanded.
Those are not the same activity, and confusing them has wrecked a lot of faith.
This is where Yom Teruah stops being a nice pattern and becomes the literal mechanism of our hope.

Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.

For the Master himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of Elohim. The dead in Messiah will rise first, then we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Master in the air.
Look at the components: a shout, a voice, a trumpet. That is a teruah with a resurrection attached to it.

But immediately after the oppression of those days... he will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.

Note the timing marker Yahshua placed himself. After the oppression of those days. The gathering happens at the trumpet, after the tribulation, not before it. This is the resurrection of the dead and the changing of the living into glorified bodies.
The seventh angel sounded, and great voices in heaven followed, saying, The kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Master, and of his Messiah. He will reign forever and ever!
The last trumpet. The seventh. The kingdom transfers at a trumpet blast.
The prophets said it first

It will happen in that day that a great trumpet will be blown; and those who were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and those who were outcasts in the land of Egypt, shall come; and they will worship YHWH in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

Do not read past that one. The great trumpet gathers the ones scattered into Assyria. That is the northern house, the tribes who were exiled and lost their identity. The trumpet is the sound that brings the outcasts home and puts the two sticks back into one hand (Ezekiel 37:15-22).
The Master YHWH will blow the trumpet, and will go with whirlwinds of the south.
Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain, for the day of YHWH comes, for it is close at hand.
Blow the trumpet in Zion. Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly.
The great day of YHWH is near. A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fortified cities.
Does the trumpet alarm sound in a city without the people being afraid?
Blow the horn in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah.
At Sinai the voice of the trumpet sounded loud and long, and grew louder and louder.
Every prophet who describes the Day of YHWH reaches for the same instrument.
Leviticus 23:24 calls it a zikhron teruah, a memorial of blowing. Memorial means remembrance, and remembrance runs in both directions.
Then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets. Then you will be remembered before YHWH your Elohim, and you will be saved from your enemies.
The trumpet is the sound of being remembered by YHWH.

Then those who feared YHWH spoke one with another; and YHWH listened and heard, and a book of memory was written before him for those who feared YHWH and who honored his name... They shall be mine, says YHWH of Armies, my own possession in the day that I make.
There is a book with names in it, and there is a day when it is opened (Daniel 7:10; Revelation 20:12). The trumpet is the sound that announces the day has come.
Here is the argument that closes the case for anyone paying attention.
The spring feasts were fulfilled to the day
Passover
Yahshua died as the lamb, on Passover. For indeed Messiah, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place. 1 Corinthians 5:7
Unleavened Bread
His body in the tomb, without corruption, without leaven. Acts 2:27
Firstfruits
He rose as the firstfruits of those who are asleep. 1 Corinthians 15:20-23
Shavuot
The Spirit poured out when the day had fully come. Acts 2:1
Four appointments. Four fulfillments. Not one of them was approximate. Every single one landed on the exact appointed day.
So what does that tell you about the fall feasts
Three remain: Trumpets, Atonement, and Tabernacles. If he kept the first four appointments to the hour, he is not going to improvise the last three.
Let no one therefore judge you in eating or drinking, or with respect to a feast day or a new moon or a Sabbath day, which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Messiah's.

Read it carefully, because this verse gets used backwards constantly. Paul does not say the appointed times are cancelled. He says do not let people judge you for keeping them, and then he says they are a shadow of things to come. Future tense, written decades after the resurrection. The shadow is still pointing at something.

sections.heading: Why Followers of Yahshua Should Keep This Day

blocks.v: Here is the case, laid out plainly, without arguing with anybody.
1. He called them his.
These are my set feasts (Leviticus 23:2). Not Jewish feasts. His. If they belong to him, and we belong to him, the question mostly answers itself.
2. They were never given only to one bloodline.

items: One law shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you. Exodus
One statute for you and for the foreigner, forever throughout your generations. Numbers 15:15-16
Let no foreigner who has joined himself to YHWH say, YHWH will surely separate me from his people. Them I will bring to my holy mountain. Isaiah 56:3, 6-7

blocks.v: 3. You have already been brought near.

You were at that time separate from Messiah, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise... But now in Messiah Yahshua you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Messiah... So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and of the household of Elohim.
You were grafted into the olive tree (Romans 11:17-24). The tree did not become yours. You became part of it. A grafted branch does not get a different calendar than the tree.
4. The first followers kept them.

items: They were gathered together on Shavuot when the Spirit fell. Acts 2:1 Paul arranged his travel around keeping the appointed times. Acts 18:21; Acts 20:16
Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old yeast, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. 1

blocks.v: That last one was written to a mostly non-Jewish congregation in Greece. Let us keep the feast.
5. Yahshua kept them, and we follow him.

items: He went up to the Feast of Tabernacles. John 7:2, 10 I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. Luke 22:15
He who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked. 1 John 2:6 If you love me, keep my commandments. John 14:15
Do not think that I came to destroy the Torah or the prophets. I did not come to destroy, but to fulfill. Matthew

blocks.v: 6. They are still being kept in the age to come.

items: Everyone who is left of all the nations will go up from year to year to worship the King and to keep the feast of

blocks.v: booths. Zechariah 14:16-19
From one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me.

items: The appointed times observed in the restored kingdom. Ezekiel 45:21-25

blocks.v: If the nations keep them in the kingdom, there is no version of this where they were abolished in between.
7. And the practical one.
You cannot watch a clock you refuse to look at. He said watch. He tied his return to a trumpet. He put a trumpet on the calendar. Keeping this day is how you stay oriented to the season.
Now the guardrail, because this is where people get hurt. Keeping a feast does not save anybody. It never did.
Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me. New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I cannot stand evil assemblies. My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts.

Stop and feel that. He is not condemning the days he himself commanded. He is condemning days kept by hands full of blood and hearts full of pride. Read the next verses. He tells them to wash, to cease from evil, to relieve the oppressed, to plead for the widow.
I hate, I despise your feasts... But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream. Amos

items: These people draw near to me with their mouth, and honor me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.
What does YHWH require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your Elohim? Micah

blocks.title: Say It Plainly
blocks.v: Do not blow a shofar and then go back to holding a grudge. Do not put on tzitzit and refuse to forgive your brother. Do not learn a Hebrew word and stay proud. That is exactly what he said he hates.
The day is an appointment with a Person. Keep the appointment, but bring your heart.
This is the thread we never want to miss, because it is the reason this ministry exists. The trumpet in Scripture is not only a warning. It is the sound of release.

Then you shall sound the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land. You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee to you; and each of you shall return to his own property, and each of you shall return to his family.
Debts cancelled. Slaves released. Property restored. Families reunited. All of it announced by a horn.
And when Yahshua stood up in the synagogue to announce his own ministry, this is the passage he reached for:

The Spirit of the Master YHWH is on me, because YHWH has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound... to proclaim the year of YHWH's favor.
The trumpet season is jubilee season. Release season. And Yahshua tied our own release directly to whether we release others.
For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses. Matthew 6:14-15

items: The servant forgiven an unpayable debt who would not release a small one, and was handed over to the

blocks.v: tormentors. Matthew 18:21-35

items: Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone. Mark 11:25

blocks.title: The Order Of Things
blocks.v: Unforgiveness is a debt you are still choosing to collect on after the trumpet has announced that the debts are cancelled. It is standing in the middle of jubilee with somebody's account still open. And underneath unforgiveness, every single time, is pride. Pride says I am owed. Pride says what they did is bigger than what I was forgiven. Humility is what lets the hand open. That is why the trumpet comes before atonement on the calendar. The alarm sounds, and then there are days to go get your heart right. If you want a real Yom Teruah, do not just hear a horn. Go release somebody.
There is one more role the trumpet belongs to, and it is not the King's. It is ours.

If, when he sees the sword come on the land, he blows the trumpet and warns the people, then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and does not heed the warning, if the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head... But if the watchman sees the sword come and does not blow the trumpet, and the people are not warned... I will require his blood at the watchman's hand.

items: Cry aloud. Do not spare. Lift up your voice like a trumpet. Isaiah 58:1 I will stand at my watch, and set myself on the ramparts, and will look out to see what he will say to me.
Watch therefore, for you do not know when the lord of the house is coming, lest coming suddenly he might find you sleeping. What I tell you, I tell all: Watch. Mark 13:34-37

blocks.v: The watchman does not know the hour either. That was never his job. His job is to be awake and to have his lips on the horn.

sections.heading: The Day They Read the Book

blocks.v: One passage almost nobody connects to this feast, and it is one of the most beautiful in Scripture.
All the people gathered themselves together as one man into the wide place... and they spoke to Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the Torah of Moses... on the first day of the seventh month.
That is Yom Teruah. They read from morning until midday. And when the people heard the instructions of YHWH after generations of exile, they wept. They realized how far they had drifted.
Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for this day is holy to our Master. Do not be grieved, for the joy of YHWH is your strength.

That is what this day looks like when it is done right. The scattered people gather. The book is opened. Hearts break over what was lost. And then joy, feasting, and portions sent to whoever has nothing prepared.
Grieve over what was lost, then eat, then go feed somebody who has nothing. That is Yom Teruah.
Straight from the text, with nothing added.
A holy convocation. Gather. Do not do this alone if you can help it. Leviticus 23:24; Hebrews 10:25
A solemn rest. No regular work. Lay the job down. Leviticus 23:24-25; Numbers 29:1
Blow the trumpet. A shofar if you have one, whatever horn you have if you do not. Make the sound. Leviticus 23:24;
Numbers 10:10; Psalm 81:3
Read the book out loud. Follow the Nehemiah 8 pattern. Leviticus 23, Numbers 10, Matthew 24 and 25, 1
Thessalonians 4 and 5, 1 Corinthians 15.
Search your heart and release your debts. Forgive before Atonement comes. Matthew 6:14-15; Leviticus 25:9-10
Eat well, and send a portion to someone who has nothing prepared. Nehemiah 8:10
What is tradition, and what is Scripture

Be honest with people about this. The name Rosh Hashanah, the ten Days of Awe, apples and honey, the specific shofar sequences, the books of life and death ceremony, and the wedding customs sometimes taught alongside this day are all tradition. Some of it is beautiful. None of it is commanded.

What is commanded is short: rest, gather, blow, and remember. Do not add a burden Scripture did not put there, and do not despise a brother who keeps a custom you do not. If one man marks the day by a sighted moon and another marks it by calculation, do not break fellowship over a sliver of light.
One man esteems one day as more important. Another esteems every day alike. Let each man be fully assured in his own mind. He who observes the day, observes it to the Master.
The point was never precision. The point is that you are watching.
The whole study in one place:

items: YHWH set appointments in the sky on day four of creation, before there was a single Hebrew on the earth.
He called them his feasts, and commanded that they be kept in their appointed season.
He put exactly one of them on the first day of a month, on the day the moon goes dark, and made it a day of shouting. The only moed nobody can pin to an hour.
He fulfilled the first four appointments in Yahshua, precisely, on the day.
Yahshua said he returns at a trumpet, after the tribulation, to gather his own and raise the dead.
He said no one knows the day or the hour.
And he said, in the same breath, that those who watch the tree will know the season, and that the day will not overtake the children of light like a thief.

blocks.v: So we do not set dates. We stay awake. We keep the appointment. We keep our lamps full. We keep our accounts released and our hands open. And when that broken, urgent, joyful sound goes up, we are not startled.

blocks.title: The Last Word
blocks.v: We are the people who know the joyful sound (Psalm 89:15). Blow the horn. Open the book. Forgive somebody. He is coming back at a trumpet, and he has never once missed an appointment.
