topics.title: Husbands, Love Your Wives
topics.subtitle: As Yahshua Loves His Bride
topics.note: A Midrash Study on Ephesians 5:22-33 Scripture quoted from the World English Bible with the sacred names restored. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of YHWH.

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Paul does not end Ephesians 5 on marriage advice. He ends it by calling marriage a great mystery that speaks about Messiah and his assembly. Marriage was never mainly about companionship. It is a living picture, walking around on the earth, of the covenant between Yahshua and his people. That is why the enemy attacks it so hard. Break the picture, and you distort what people believe about YHWH himself.

Subjecting yourselves to one another in the fear of Messiah. Wives, be subject to your own husbands, as to Yahshua. For the husband is the head of the wife, as Messiah also is the head of the assembly, being himself the savior of the body. Husbands, love your wives, even as Messiah also loved the assembly, and gave himself up for it, that he might sanctify it, having cleansed it by the washing of water with the word, that he might present the assembly to himself glorious, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that it should be holy and without defect. Even so husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself. For no man ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, even as Yahshua also does the assembly. For this cause a man will leave his father and mother and will be joined to his wife. Then the two will become one flesh. This mystery is great, but I speak concerning Messiah and of the assembly.

Notice where Paul lands. Everything he just said about a husband and a wife turns out to be a picture of Yahshua and his bride. Read the passage without that ending and it becomes a list of household rules. Read it with that ending and it becomes a revelation of how YHWH loves his people.
Read what Paul actually asks of the husband. He does not say love her as much as you can. He does not say love her the way she loves you. He does not say love her while she deserves it.
He says: love her the way Yahshua loved the assembly. And how did Yahshua love the assembly? He gave himself up for it.
But Elohim commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Messiah died for us.
That is the standard. He died for a bride who was not yet cleaned up, not yet respectful, not yet grateful. He did not wait for her to become worthy. He made her worthy by loving her first.
We love him, because he first loved us.

blocks.title: Say It Plainly
blocks.v: Husband, you go first. Every time. Not because she earned it. Not because she asked correctly. Because that is what your Head did for you while you were still his enemy.

sections.heading: The Backdrop: YHWH Has Always Been a Husband

blocks.v: Ephesians 5 is not new material. Paul is standing on the whole Tanakh. YHWH has described himself as a husband from the beginning.
My covenant they broke, although I was a husband to them, says YHWH.
For your Maker is your husband. YHWH of Armies is his name.
As the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your Elohim will rejoice over you.
I will betroth you to me forever, in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion.
I will allure her, bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her.
He covers her nakedness, enters covenant, washes her with water, anoints her with oil, clothes her, adorns her, and makes her beauty perfect.
You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.
I remember for you the kindness of your youth, the love of your weddings.
He gives faithless Israel a certificate of divorce for covenant breaking. Covenant is real, and breaking it is real.
Sinai Was a Wedding
Look at Exodus 19 through 24 with wedding eyes:

items: YHWH comes down to meet the people. Exodus 19:11
The people wash their garments and set themselves apart for three days, the bridal immersion. Exodus 19:10, 14
He speaks the terms of the covenant, the ketubah, his instructions.
The people answer, all that YHWH has spoken we will do. That is the bride saying I do. Exodus 19:8; 24:3, 7
The covenant is confirmed with blood, and the elders eat and drink before him, the covenant meal. Exodus 24:8,

blocks.v: His instructions are not a legal code handed down to slaves. They are the marriage covenant a Husband gave to a bride he had just rescued out of Egypt. That reframes everything. Obedience is how you love the one you are in covenant with, not a burden laid on you by a distant judge.
If you love me, keep my commandments.
Yahshua followed the ancient wedding pattern exactly. Every husband should know this, because it shows the shape of covenant love.
1. The price is paid.
You were bought with a price (1 Corinthians 6:20). You were redeemed with the precious blood of Messiah (1 Peter 1:18-19). The bridegroom paid the mohar to the father before he ever took her home.
2. The covenant is cut over a cup.
This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you (Luke 22:20). He lifted the cup, she drank, and they were bound. That is betrothal, and betrothal was already full covenant.
3. He goes to prepare a place.

In my Father's house are many homes. If it weren't so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you. If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will receive you to myself.
The groom went home and built onto his father's house. He did not come back until the father said it was finished.
4. No one knows the day or hour.

No one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but the Father only (Matthew 24:36). That is not mystery for its own sake. That is the wedding custom: the father decides when the house is ready.
5. He returns with a shout and a trumpet.

items: At midnight there was a cry, behold, the bridegroom is coming, come out to meet him. Matthew 25:6
With a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of Elohim. 1 Thessalonians 4:16
He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones.

blocks.v: 6. The wedding supper.

Let us rejoice and be exceedingly glad, for the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready (Revelation 19:7-9). She comes down prepared as a bride adorned for her husband (Revelation 21:2).

Paul saw himself standing inside this pattern as the friend of the bridegroom: I betrothed you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Messiah (2 Corinthians 11:2). John said the same, the friend of the bridegroom rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom's voice (John 3:29).

blocks.title: Apply It
blocks.v: You are in a betrothal, not a transaction. You did not buy her the way Yahshua bought you, but you are still called to spend yourself on her the same way: pay first, prepare a place, and keep the covenant while you wait.

sections.heading: The Five Verbs: How Yahshua Loves

blocks.v: This is the spine of the whole study. Paul does not leave love her like Messiah undefined. He gives five specific actions in Ephesians 5:25-29.
1. He GAVE HIMSELF UP
Ephesians 5:25
The first move of headship is death, not leadership.

items: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends. John 15:13
The Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many. Matthew 20:28
He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, and humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death.

blocks.v: Most husbands are willing to die for their wives in theory. Take a bullet. Run into a burning house. Very few are willing to die daily in the small places: die to being right, die to the last word, die to the evening you had planned, die to the hobby, die to the phone, die to your own comfort. Yahshua did not only die for her. He lived giving himself up for her, every single day, until the day he did it publicly.
2. He SANCTIFIES her, he sets her apart
Ephesians 5:26
To sanctify is to set apart for one purpose only. He does not share her. He does not compare her. He does not put her in a lineup.

Practically, she is set apart from every other woman in your life: from the ones on the screen, from the one at work who laughs at your jokes, from your mother's expectations, from your past. Set apart also means set above your calling, your business, and even your ministry.

items: You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. Exodus 20:17
Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife of your youth. Proverbs 5:18 I made a covenant with my eyes. How then should I look lustfully at a young woman. Job 31:1

blocks.v: 3. He CLEANSES her with the washing of water with the word
Ephesians 5:26
This is the bridal immersion. It is Ezekiel 16:9 all over again: then I washed you with water. The husband is the one who washes his wife with the word.

blocks.title: A Warning To Husbands
blocks.v: Washing is gentle. Washing removes what is not hers. Washing is something you do kneeling down, for the good of the one you are caring for.
The word in your hand is a basin of water for her, not a club to correct her with. If she flinches when you open Scripture, you have turned the washing into a beating.
What washing actually looks like:
Praying over her out loud, by name, in her hearing. Speaking Scripture over her identity, not over her failures.

items: Covering her in prayer before she ever asks you to.
Reminding her what YHWH says about her on the day she has forgotten.

blocks.v: Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth (John 17:17).
4. He PRESENTS her glorious, without spot or wrinkle
Ephesians 5:27
Yahshua does not look at his bride and see her current condition. He sees the finished woman he is going to present.

He called Simon a rock while Simon was still unstable enough to deny him three times (John 1:42; Matthew 16:18). He called Gideon a mighty man of valor while Gideon was hiding in a winepress from the Midianites
(Judges 6:12).

blocks.title: Ask Yourself
blocks.v: Do you speak to your wife's condition, or to her calling? Your words are prophetic in your home. She will very often grow into whatever you keep calling her, for good or for evil. Death and life are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21).
5. He NOURISHES and CHERISHES her
Ephesians 5:29
These are present tense, ongoing words. The stake was once. The nourishing and cherishing is every day.

items: Nourish means to feed, to provide, to cause to grow: spiritually, emotionally, and physically.
Cherish means literally to warm with body heat, the way a bird covers her young.

blocks.v: Provision without warmth is not this command. A man can pay every bill in the house and never once cherish his wife. Cold provision is not love. It is management.

You husbands, in the same way, live with your wives according to knowledge, giving honor to the woman as to the weaker vessel, as also being joint heirs of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.
For the husband is the head of the wife, as Messiah also is the head of the assembly, being himself the savior of the body.

Paul defines headship in the same breath he states it: savior of the body. Head means the one who goes first into the danger, not the one who sits highest at the table. And Yahshua drew the line himself.

You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you, but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant.

Every worldly definition of headship is exactly what Yahshua forbade. If your leadership looks like the rulers of the nations, issuing orders, demanding compliance, keeping score, then you are not leading like the Head. You are leading like Babylon.

Notice also the verse that governs the entire passage, the one sitting right before it begins: subjecting yourselves to one another in the fear of Messiah (Ephesians 5:21). That is the header over the whole household section. Mutual submission comes first, and everything after it is worked out underneath it.
Headship is also not superiority. Yahshua submits to the Father (1 Corinthians 11:3; 15:28) and is fully YHWH. Order of function is never a statement of worth.
Even so husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself. For no man ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it.

This flows straight out of the design. A man will leave his father and his mother, and will join to his wife, and they will be one flesh (Genesis 2:24). They are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore Elohim has joined together, let no man tear apart (Matthew 19:6).

If you are one flesh, then every cutting word you speak to her is self harm. You would not starve your own arm. You would not mock your own leg in front of your friends. You would not ignore an infection in your own hand for years and call it her problem. The wound you leave in her is a wound in you. That is not poetry. That is the mechanics of one flesh.
The Side of Adam and the Side of Yahshua
YHWH Elohim caused a deep sleep to fall on the man, and he slept. He took one of his ribs, and made a woman, and brought her to the man.
One of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.

Adam fell into a deep sleep, his side was opened, and out of the wound came his bride. Yahshua fell into the sleep of death, his side was opened, and out came blood and water: the blood that redeems her, and the water that washes her, exactly as Ephesians 5:26 says.

blocks.title: The Picture
blocks.v: The bride comes out of the opened side of the man. She was never taken from his foot to be walked on, and never from his head to rule over him. She came from his side, from under his arm, close to his heart.

sections.heading: Examples: How Yahshua Actually Treated People

blocks.v: Paul says to love her as Messiah loved. So let us look at what he actually did. Every one of these is a direct pattern for a husband.
1. He washed feet. John 13:1-17

Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end. Knowing all authority was in his hands, he got up, took a towel, and washed dirt off feet, including the feet of the man about to betray him.
Husband: What is the towel in your house? What is the job nobody sees?
2. He served before he was thanked. Luke 17:11-19
He healed ten lepers. One came back. He healed them anyway.
Husband: Love that requires a thank you is a transaction.
3. He knew her whole history and did not shame her. John 4:1-29
The woman at the well had five husbands and was living with a man. He named the truth without weaponizing it, gave her living water, and made her the first witness to her city.
Husband: Knowing her failures is not permission to bring them up.
4. He stood between her and the accusers. John 8:1-11
He put his own body between a guilty woman and the stones. Then he said, neither do I condemn you, go your way, from now on sin no more.
Husband: Do you stand between your wife and the accusation, including your own tongue?
5. He prayed for Peter before Peter failed. Luke 22:31-32
I prayed for you, that your faith would not fail. He interceded before the fall instead of condemning after it.
Husband: Are you praying about her weak place, or complaining about it?
6. He wept with them before he fixed anything. John 11:32-35
He was about to raise Lazarus in ten minutes. He wept first.
Husband: She usually does not want the solution yet. She wants you in the grief with her first.
7. He would not break what was already bent. Isaiah 42:3; Matthew 12:20
He will not break a bruised reed. He will not quench a smoking wick.
Husband: When she is already at her weakest, that is the moment to be gentlest, not the moment to make your point.
8. He did not quarrel or raise his voice in the street. Isaiah 42:2; Matthew 12:19
He did not strive, nor cry out, and no one heard his voice in the streets.
Husband: Volume is not authority. A raised voice in a marriage is a confession that you have run out of self control.
9. He forgave while he was still being wronged. Luke 23:34
Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing. The nails were still in his hands.
Husband: He did not wait for an apology, and neither can you.
10. He restored the one who failed him publicly. John 21:9-17
Peter denied him three times. Yahshua cooked him breakfast on a beach and asked, do you love me, three times. One restoration for every denial.
Husband: Full restoration, not probation. Not held over her head for years.
11. He carried her burden instead of adding to it. Matthew 11:28-30
Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened. My yoke is easy and my burden is light.
Husband: Is your house a place she can rest, or one more place she has to perform?
12. He honored the woman the room called wasteful. Mark 14:3-9
When they criticized the woman with the alabaster jar, he defended her out loud. Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her?
Husband: Defend her in the room, correct in private. Never the other way around.
Exodus 21:10

Even a man who took a second wife could not diminish the first wife's food, clothing, or marital rights. YHWH set a floor under how a woman is to be treated. Provision, covering, and intimacy are her right, not her reward.
Deuteronomy 24:5

A newly married man goes to no war and carries no business obligation for one full year, and shall cheer his wife whom he has taken. The Creator built a protected year of undistracted attention into his instructions. If he guarded the first year like that, what do you suppose he thinks of a man who gives his wife his leftovers for thirty years?
Malachi 2:13-16 and 1 Peter 3:7

The men in Malachi were weeping at the altar because YHWH would not accept their offerings. Why? YHWH has been witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion and the wife of your covenant. Their worship was rejected because of how they treated their wives.

Peter says the same thing on the other side of the resurrection: live with her according to knowledge, give her honor, remember she is a joint heir of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.

blocks.title: Two Witnesses
blocks.v: Two witnesses, one on each side of the stake, saying the same thing: how you treat your wife directly affects your standing in prayer and worship.
You cannot be right with YHWH and wrong with her. There is no such thing as a powerful man of prayer who is a tyrant at home. That man is deceiving himself.

items: Colossians 3:19. Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter against them. Bitterness is named as the husband's specific sin. It is what unforgiveness becomes when it is allowed to sit. 1 Corinthians 7:3-5. Mutual authority, mutual obligation, and no withholding from one another except by agreement for a season of prayer.
Proverbs 5:18-19. Rejoice, delight, and be captivated by the wife of your youth. Delight is commanded, not optional.

Proverbs 31:28-29. Her husband also praises her. Out loud, where people can hear it. 1 Corinthians 13:4-8. Read it with her name in mind. Patient, kind, not jealous, not proud, not rude, not self seeking, not provoked, keeps no record of wrongs, bears all things, never fails.

sections.heading: Where It Actually Breaks: Pride and Forgiveness

blocks.v: Here is the honest part, and it is the heart of everything we teach at Kingdom Life.
Almost no marriage dies from one big event. Marriages die from a stack of unforgiven small things: offenses filed away, kept on a list, pulled back out in every argument, held as leverage.
And unforgiveness is never the root. Pride is the root. Unforgiveness is what pride looks like when it is wearing a wound as a costume.

Pride says: what she did was too big, I have a right to hold this, she has to come to me first, I have to protect myself. Pride is sneaky. It will disguise itself as boundaries, as discernment, as being the spiritual one in the house, as I have forgiven her, I just do not trust her. It will let a man sit in bitterness for a decade and call it wisdom.

blocks.title: The Order Of Things
blocks.v: Humility is the root of forgiveness. Forgiveness is the root of deliverance.

If you want deliverance in your house, it starts with you forgiving her completely, out loud, without conditions, and then humbling yourself enough to ask her forgiveness for what you have done. Not a general apology. Specific. That is where chains break.
If you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses. Matthew 6:14-15

items: Be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as Elohim also in Messiah forgave you.

blocks.v: Forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any, even as Messiah forgave you, so you also do.

items: Elohim resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble. James 4:6
Do not let the sun go down on your wrath, and do not give place to the devil. Ephesians 4:26-27

blocks.v: That last one is a warning about legal ground. Anger held overnight, night after night, becomes an open door. Many men are fighting torment in their own homes that they themselves let in through years of unforgiveness toward the woman sleeping next to them.
Truth in love means saying this part plainly.

items: Headship is not control. Yahshua never once forced his bride. He invites, he serves, he waits. A man who uses Ephesians 5 to demand compliance has inverted the passage. Paul gave the wife one verse and the husband nine. Submission is not obedience to sin or to abuse. As to Yahshua, in verse 22, is a limit, not a blank check. Nothing in Scripture requires a woman to submit to being harmed. A man who is harming his wife has already broken the covenant he is appealing to.
Her submission is not the condition of your love. Verse 25 has no if in it. Messiah loved her while she was still a sinner, and you are not permitted to wait.

Loving her is not weakness. It took more strength for Yahshua to stay on the stake than it would have taken to call twelve legions of angels (Matthew 26:53). Restraint under provocation is the strongest thing a man does.
This is not about being perfect. It is about direction. Repenting and returning, over and over, is the walk.

blocks.v: Practical, testable, and small enough to actually do. Seven days.
Wash her once a day. Pray over her out loud, by name, in her hearing. Not about her. Over her.
Take the towel. Do one thing she normally does, without being asked, and without mentioning it afterward.
Name her calling, not her condition. Tell her one true thing about who she is becoming.
Forgive one specific thing. Say it to YHWH out loud, release it, and then never bring it up again. Not in an argument,
not as a joke.
Ask her forgiveness for one specific thing. No but. No if I. Name it and ask.
Cherish, do not just provide. Warmth costs time, not money. Sit with her with nothing in your hands.
Defend her in the room. Publicly, once, where she can hear it.

topics.title: Why We Don't Eat Pig
topics.subtitle: The Instruction, the Evidence, and the Grace to Turn Around
topics.lede: YHWH never told Israel why. He did not owe them a reason, and He does not owe us one. But when we do look, we find that He drew a line around the one animal whose flesh our own medicine treats as the closest working stand in for ours.
topics.note: A printable teaching handout. Scripture quoted from the World English Bible with the Names restored: YHWH, Yahshua, Elohim. Torah is referred to throughout as instructions, which is what the word means. Every scientific claim in this handout is linked to its source, so you can check it yourself.

blocks.v: YHWH never told Israel why. He did not owe them a reason, and He does not owe us one. Our obedience was never supposed to wait on a study confirming it. But when we do look, we find that He drew a line around the one animal whose flesh our own medicine treats as the closest working stand in for ours.

items: The instruction itself, in Leviticus and Deuteronomy, with no reason attached.
Why this was never a health code, and how clean and unclean were known long before Sinai.
The prophets naming pig's flesh centuries later, in judgment language, not food safety language.
Every passage used to say pork was made clean, answered one at a time.
What modern science has found about pig flesh and human flesh, with sources linked.
How to say it carefully, including where the claim is strong and where it is not.
Grace for everyone who has eaten it, which is most of us.
Answers to the pushback you will actually hear.

sections.heading: The Instruction, With No Reason Attached

blocks.v: The clean and unclean instructions are given in two places, and both name the pig specifically.
“The pig, because it has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, is unclean to you. You shall not eat their meat. You shall not touch their carcasses. They are unclean to you.”
“The pig, because it has a split hoof but doesn’t chew the cud, is unclean to you. You shall not eat their meat. You shall not touch their carcasses.”

Notice what is missing. No explanation. No health warning. No reason offered at all. The standard is not what the animal has been through, it is what the animal is. A creature that chews the cud and has a split hoof is clean. The pig has the hoof and not the cud, so it is out.
Notice something else. The instruction goes past eating. Do not touch their carcasses. That is not a rule about digestion. That is a rule about separation.
Israel obeyed without knowing why. We are the generation that gets to read the lab reports.
And the chapter tells you the purpose, even while withholding the reason.
“For I am YHWH your God. Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am holy … You shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.”

Set apart. That is what holy means. He set His people apart in what they carried in their bodies, not only in what they carried in their hearts. Peter quotes those very words to believers in 1 Peter 1:15-16, long after the resurrection.

sections.heading: This Was Never a Health Code

blocks.v: The most common defense of pork is that the danger was parasites, and modern processing solved it. That answers a question YHWH never raised.

items: If the problem were parasites, the instruction would have been to cook it. They knew how to cook meat in 1400 BC. He regulated other things by preparation. With the pig He did not regulate the preparation, He called the animal itself unclean.
Processing changes the condition of the meat. It does not change what the animal is. A clean animal is clean before anyone processes anything.
He never revised it when butchering improved. Centuries later the prophets are still naming pig's flesh, and food safety is nowhere in view.

blocks.v: There is also a timing problem for the idea that this was a temporary rule for one nation. Clean and unclean were already known long before Sinai, and before there was an Israel to give it to.
“You shall take seven pairs of every clean animal with you, the male and his female. Of the animals that are not clean, take two, the male and his female.”

This is Noah, roughly eight hundred years before Moses. YHWH tells him to take clean animals by sevens and unclean by twos, and gives no definition. He does not have to. Noah already knew the difference.
If this were only about a wilderness generation and their kitchens, it would not resurface in the prophets. It does, and in the strongest language in Scripture.

“I have spread out my hands all day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts … who sit among the graves, and spend nights in secret places; who eat pig’s meat, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels.”

“Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves to go to the gardens, following one in the middle, eating pig’s meat, abominable things, and the mouse, they shall come to an end together,” says YHWH.

Read Isaiah 66:17 in context. This is the closing chapter of Isaiah, and it is describing the end, when YHWH comes to gather the nations and set His glory among them. Pig's flesh is named there. Not in a health warning, and not in a list of temporary ordinances. In a judgment.

Isaiah 66:3 puts the offering of pig's blood alongside idolatry. The issue in these passages is people going their own way while calling themselves sanctified. Eating what He set apart from is treated as the visible evidence of it.

A note on the reference, because it comes up. The verse about those who eat swine's flesh being consumed at His return is Isaiah 66:17, not Isaiah 63. Isaiah 63 is the day of vengeance and the winepress. Get the citation right and no one gets to dismiss the point on a technicality.
blocks.title: Get the citation right

sections.heading: The Passages Used to Say Pork Was Made Clean

blocks.v: Before working through them, notice what is not there. No verse says the pig is now clean. No verse says the instruction was repealed. What exists is a set of passages about other subjects, stretched to imply it.
Mark 7:1-23
The claim: Yahshua declared all foods clean.

items: Read verse 2 and verse 5. The subject of the whole passage is stated twice: the disciples ate with unwashed hands. That is a tradition of the elders, not an instruction from YHWH. Verse 8 names the actual problem: you set aside the commandment of God to hold your tradition.
The phrase in verse 19 is a translator's parenthesis in most modern versions, and it follows a sentence about digestion. Whatever goes into the mouth passes into the stomach and out into the latrine.

The word food already meant food. Nobody at that table considered pig to be food. To a first century Jewish audience, declaring foods clean means the clean things you eat with unwashed hands are still clean. It does not silently add the swine to the menu.

The passage ends where it began. Verses 21 to 23 list what actually defiles a man, and it is a list of sins, then verse 23 closes the argument about the heart. Not one word about the dietary instructions.

blocks.v: Acts 10, Peter's vision
The claim: YHWH told Peter to kill and eat, so pork is clean.

items: Peter refuses, and says he has never eaten anything unclean. This is years after the resurrection. If the instruction had been cancelled at the cross, the closest disciple to Yahshua never got the notice.

Peter himself interprets the vision, and Scripture records his interpretation so we would not have to guess. Acts 10:28: God has shown me that I should not call any man unholy or unclean. Acts 10:34: God does not show favoritism.
The whole chapter is about Cornelius, a Gentile. Three men are at the door before the vision ends. The vision was about who Peter could walk into, not what he could put on his plate.

blocks.v: 1 Timothy 4:1-5
The claim: Every creature is good and nothing is to be refused.

items: Read verse 3. Paul is describing false teachers who forbid marriage and command abstaining from foods. That is asceticism. Torah does not forbid marriage, so this cannot be a description of Torah keepers.
Verse 3 also limits the subject: foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth. The pig was never created to be received as food.

Verse 5 gives the test: it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer. Take it back to the word of God and the word of God says the pig is unclean. Prayer does not overrule the text it is appealing to.

blocks.v: Romans 14

items: The dispute in the chapter is between one who eats all things and one who eats only vegetables. Nobody in Scripture was ever told to eat only vegetables. This is a meat sold to idols and personal conviction question in a mixed congregation, not a repeal of Leviticus 11.
The pig is never mentioned in the chapter.
Paul does not contradict Paul. In Acts 24:14 he says he believes all things written in the instructions and the prophets, and in Acts 25:8 he says he has committed no offense against them.

blocks.v: Colossians 2:16, 1 Corinthians 10:25, Genesis 9:3

rows.v: Paul says do not let anyone judge you for what you eat and drink and for the appointed times. He is defending the ones keeping them, not the ones abstaining. Verses 8 and 22 name the real problem: the tradition and commandments of men.
Meat sold in the marketplace, and the question of meat offered to idols. The Corinthian market question was whether it had been in a temple, not whether it was swine.

Given to Noah, the same man who had just been told to load clean animals by sevens and unclean by twos, two chapters earlier. Whatever this verse permits, Noah did not understand it as erasing a distinction he had just been given.

The four requirements were a starting point for brand new Gentile believers, not a completed curriculum. Verse 21 says why: Moses is read in the synagogues every Sabbath, where they would learn the rest.

blocks.v: Every one of these passages is about something else. Not one of them says the pig is clean. You have to bring that conclusion to the text, because you cannot get it out of the text.

None of this is the reason for the instruction. It is a witness that lines up with it. Every finding below is linked to its source. Check them yourself, and do not repeat any claim you have not looked at.
Transplants: medicine reaches for the pig

Pig tissue is not experimental. It is routine. Roughly 60,000 patients in the United States every year receive heart valve replacements made from pig tissue, and those valves last around fifteen years (Understanding Animal Research).

In March 2024 a surgical team in China transplanted a six gene edited pig liver into a human recipient. It produced bile and pig albumin, held stable blood flow, and showed no sign of rejection across a ten day observation window. The study was published in Nature in 2025 (Tao et al., Nature 2025). Say this one accurately: the recipient was brain dead, and the pig liver was placed alongside the native liver rather than replacing it. It is still the first peer reviewed pig liver in a human body, and it still worked.
When modern medicine needs a stand in for human flesh, it does not reach for a cow, a sheep, a deer, or a goat. It reaches for the pig.
Genetics: the pig carries our genes
A 2025 USDA study in BMC Genomics manually assembled and annotated the pig proteome and compared pig, mouse, and human (Dawson et al., BMC Genomics 2025). Its findings:

items: NCBI lists roughly 20,790 protein coding genes in pigs and 20,080 in humans. Nearly identical counts.
When a gene is missing from one of the three genomes, pigs are 5.0 times more likely than mice to carry the human version.
When a functional domain is missing from a protein in one of the three species, pigs are 2 times more likely than mice to have the human domain.
Pigs can produce roughly 90 percent of the human transcript variants tested, and pig to human mRNA conservation averages about 75 percent.

blocks.v: Immune system: we speak nearly the same language

Of the 419 CD immune markers catalogued in humans, researchers have identified 359 corresponding proteins in pigs (Dawson and Lunney, 2018). More broadly, the porcine immune system resembles the human immune system in more than 80 percent of measured parameters, compared to about 10 percent for the mouse (Pabst, Cell and Tissue Research 2020).
Skin: close enough to graft

Pig skin and human skin share general structure, thickness, hair follicle content, pigmentation, collagen and lipid composition, which is why the pig is the standard model for wound healing, burns, transdermal drug delivery, and dermal toxicity testing (Summerfield, Meurens and Ricklin, Molecular Immunology 2015). Both pig and human skin are fixed skin, attached to the tissue underneath, unlike rodent skin which is loose.
Fat and metabolism

The pig is used as a model for human obesity and metabolic syndrome because it is omnivorous like we are, tends toward sedentary behavior and fattening like we do, and shares metabolic and cardiovascular features with us (swine metabolic syndrome study, PMC3354447). Not one of the other clean animals named in Leviticus 11 sits in that seat.
Truth does not need exaggeration, and one overstated claim will cost you the whole conversation. Here is where the line is.

items: Do not say the pig is the closest genetic match to humans. It is not. Apes and primates are genetically closer, and that is not in dispute. The first person who knows it will use it to throw out everything else you said.

Say functional match instead. No surgeon puts a chimpanzee valve in a human chest. No hospital grafts monkey skin onto a burn ward patient. The pig is the animal our own medicine treats as nearly interchangeable with us at the operating table. That claim is true, verifiable, and it hits harder.

Do not claim the differences do not exist. They do. Burned pig skin does not behave mechanically like burned human skin (Gallagher et al., Scientific Reports 2022), and pig skin differs from human skin in stratum corneum thickness and blood vessel density. Naming the limits yourself is what makes the rest of it credible.
Do not build the instruction on the science. If every finding here were reversed tomorrow, Leviticus 11:7 would still read exactly the same.

blocks.v: Obedience that waits for scientific permission is not obedience. It is negotiation.
He never told them why. He did not owe them a reason, and He does not owe us one. That has to be settled first, because our obedience was never supposed to be contingent on a study confirming it.

But when we do look, when the microscopes finally catch up, we do not find an arbitrary rule. We find a Father who drew a line around the one animal whose flesh most closely mirrors the flesh of the man He made in His own image.
“God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.”

The instructions were never a scoreboard. They are an invitation. A Father telling His children what is good for them and what is not. Science is only now arriving where Torah has been standing the whole time.
Hear this clearly. There is no condemnation waiting for you here.
Most of us ate pork our entire lives. We ate it at church potlucks. We ate it on Resurrection Sunday. We did not know, and YHWH is not standing over you with a record of every breakfast.
You do not obey to become His. You obey because you already are.
Repentance is not shame. It is just turning around. And the turn can start today, with the next meal, without a single argument won and without anyone else's permission.
“Modern processing killed the parasites.”

Processing answers a health objection that was never made. He did not say the pig would make you sick. He said the animal is unclean. Processing changes the condition of the meat. It does not change what the animal is. And if heat had solved it, the instruction would have been cook it well, not do not touch it.
“What God has cleansed, do not call common.”
Peter says that about people, and Scripture lets him tell you so himself in Acts 10:28. Read the verse he explains it with before you use the verse he heard in a trance.
“It is what comes out of the mouth that defiles.”

Yahshua said that while correcting a hand washing tradition, and He listed what He meant: evil thoughts, adultery, theft, murder, pride. He was not handing out a new grocery list. And the man who said it kept Torah perfectly His whole life. If He had eaten pig, He would have sinned, and we would have no Savior.
“You are being legalistic.”

Answer this one from the heart, not the argument. We are not saved by a diet. We are saved by the blood of Yahshua. We eat this way because we love Him, and because He said what He said and no man has the authority to unsay it. A gift is not legalism.
“Then why did He make pigs at all?”
He made plenty He never told us to eat. A vulture is not a failure of design. Pigs clear the ground of what dies on it, and there is no verse anywhere that says every animal was made to be dinner.
When to stop talking

If someone has already been handed the research and reached for the first thing that let them keep the bacon, more evidence will harden them. Take it back to what YHWH actually said, say it once, and love them. Their obedience is not your job. Their hearing it clearly is.

items: He named the pig specifically, twice, and gave no reason.
The standard is what the animal is, not what condition it is in.
Clean and unclean were known in Noah's day, centuries before Sinai.
The prophets were still naming pig's flesh centuries later, in judgment, not in food safety.
Not one passage in the Renewed Covenant says the pig is clean. Every verse used is about something else.
Our own medicine treats pig flesh as the closest working stand in for human flesh on earth.
And none of that is the reason. The reason is that He said so.

And the MYH4 muscle gene study, which actually documents a difference rather than a similarity: humans do not express that gene and pigs do. Citing it hands the argument away.
